idempotencyKey.description: Optional exactly-once key for creating a sandbox. Send your own opaque, account-unique value (a UUID) to make `POST /sandboxes` safe to retry when the response is lost (network timeout, 5xx): the first request creates the sandbox and binds it to the key; every later request with the **same account, key, and request body** returns that same sandbox instead of creating a second, billable one. Behavior: keys are retained for **24 hours**; a concurrent or early retry while the first sandbox is still being minted returns `409` `idempotency_in_progress` (retry shortly, same key); reusing a key with a **different body** returns `409` `idempotency_key_reused`; timeouts and 5xx are safe to retry with the same key; a create that fails before the sandbox exists releases the key within ~2 minutes so a retry can create the sandbox. Omit the header to keep the default (non-idempotent) behavior.

type.description: Machine size. `small` consumes machine time at half rate and `large` at twice the default rate (see the Billing guide). `xlarge` needs the $100/month plan or higher, or an account access grant from an administrator. Otherwise, create, resume and fork return 403 `machine_class_plan_required`. A fork inherits the source sandbox's type unless the fork request passes its own, and resume and fork can move a sandbox between sizes.

ttlSeconds.description: Number of seconds before automatic archival. `null` disables auto-stop. The backend also accepts the string `infinite` for legacy compatibility; new clients should send null.

labels.description: Key-value labels, for example your session id. Filter on them with `GET /sandboxes?label=key=value`. At most 20 labels. Keys match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,62}`; values are strings of at most 256 bytes.

env.description: Per-sandbox environment variables injected into the sandbox's tool environment, on top of the account environment's variables (per-sandbox values win on conflicts). Keys must match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}`; at most 100 variables and 64KB total. Reserved names (`ASCII_TOKEN`, `ASCII_API_URL`, `AGENT_ID`, `PRODUCT_MODE`, `ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `BOAT_ID`, `SERVICE_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, `BOAT_CLI_TOKEN`) are rejected with `invalid_env`. Forked sandboxes inherit the source sandbox's env unless the fork request supplies its own `env`.

environment.description: Name of the sandbox environment to attach to this sandbox. Environments are managed in the Boat dashboard and bundle the repositories, secrets, and credential toggles a sandbox gets. Omit to use your default environment (`base` unless you changed it). Unknown names are rejected with `unknown_environment`. An environment marked "safe for third parties" passes nothing to the sandbox, exactly like `noEnv`.

noEnv.description: Create a sandbox with none of the secrets attached to your account (no environment variables, secret files, or credentials), confined to itself so it cannot act on your account or other sandboxes. For sandboxes you give to your own users. SSH, SCP, desktop, snapshots, and public URLs still work; pass `env` to give the sandbox a secret of its own. A fork of a no-env sandbox is always no-env. Equivalent to attaching an environment marked "safe for third parties".

snapshots.description: Pass `false` to never snapshot this sandbox. Nothing is captured in the background, so it pays no CPU or memory for it, and stopping it erases its disk the way zero data retention does. It cannot be resumed, forked, or saved as a saved snapshot, and if its machine fails there is no backup to rebuild it from.

monitoring.description: Pass `false` for monitoring off. Boat keeps no command or process output, process list or CPU/RAM samples for this sandbox, and its history, processes and metrics calls answer 409 `monitoring_off`. Live output of a running command still works. While the account default is on, `true` is refused with 409 `monitoring_off_for_account`.

failFast.description: Pass `true` to get a sandbox only if a machine of this type is ready right now. The call answers within about 1.5 s: either the usual `202` with the sandbox, or `503` `no_ready_machine` with nothing created, billed, or counted against your start limits, so you can retry or fall back at once. Without it, a create waits for a machine to be built when none is ready. Works with `from`; fork and resume take it too.

count.description: With `from`: create this many sandboxes from the saved snapshot in one request. Boat creates them together, which is faster than separate creates when you need many sandboxes at once. Start limits and the active-sandbox limit count every sandbox of the batch; if the batch does not fit, nothing is created. The answer lists all of them in `sandboxes` (and the first one in `sandbox`). Refused with 400 `count_requires_from` without `from`, and with 400 `count_with_fail_fast` together with `failFast`.

setupScript.description: Shell script that runs on the sandbox after it is ready. Ready means "ready to accept the user", not "setup done": the script starts in the background once provisioning completes and never blocks the sandbox becoming usable. It runs as the sandbox user (`user`, not root; `sudo` needs no password) via `bash`, with the sandbox's environment applied, and its output goes to a log file on the sandbox. Observe the outcome as `setupStatus` (pending/running/done/failed) and `setupError` on the sandbox. Rejected with a 400 `invalid_setup_script` error when it is not a string or exceeds 64KB. When the request also has `files`, the script starts after every file is written.

name.description: Display name of the sandbox, the same value `PATCH /sandboxes/{id}` sets. A sandbox created `from` a saved snapshot is named after the snapshot when this is omitted.

visibility.description: Who can use a sandbox billed to an organization, with the same rules as the sandbox's `visibility` field. `private`: only you can use it. `shared`: every member can, as long as it holds none of your personal logins (`noEnv`, or an environment that passes nothing). Omitted, the organization's default for new sandboxes applies (`PATCH /orgs/{org}` `newSandboxesPrivate`). It is set before the sandbox gets a machine, so a `private` sandbox is never shared, not even for a moment, and needs no `unshare` call. A personal sandbox is always private: `shared` is refused with 400 `not_org_sandbox`. Change it later with `POST /sandboxes/{id}/share` and `POST /sandboxes/{id}/unshare`.

hostedPorts.description: Ports to host on public HTTPS URLs, each exactly as `POST /sandboxes/{id}/host` does. The create waits for the sandbox's machine (up to 60 s, usually under a second), hosts every port at once and answers the URLs in `hostedPorts`. The ports are routed before the sandbox is ready, so a service that starts later is reachable as soon as it listens. Refused with 400 `invalid_hosted_ports` for a bad entry or a duplicate port, with 400 `count_with_hosted_ports` together with `count`, and with 400 `fail_fast_with_hosted_ports` together with `failFast`.

files.description: Files to write on the sandbox, each like `PUT /sandboxes/{id}/files` (a path under `/home/user` or `/tmp`, relative paths resolve against `/home/user`; missing folders are created). Boat writes them once the sandbox's disk is in place and before it reports `ready`, so a client that sees `ready`, and the `setupScript`, always find them. They are written once, at the first start: a resume does not write them again. At most 256KB in total; upload bigger files with `POST /sandboxes/{id}/files/upload-url`. `setupStatus` covers them: it stays `pending` until they are written, and a write that fails sets it `failed` with the path and the reason in `setupError` (the setup script then does not run). Refused with 400 `invalid_files` for a bad path, a duplicate path or a body over the limits.

org.description: Bill this sandbox to an organization you belong to (its shared wallet), by id or by name as `GET /orgs` lists it; `personal` or your own account id means personal billing. Omitted, the `X-Boat-Org` / `?org=` request scope applies, then the account's active wallet (`PATCH /orgs/active`), then personal. Listing, snapshots, and environments stay yours: the org is a wallet, not a shared workspace. Takes precedence over `teamId`.

Also accepts a share code (`bsh_...`) that another account made with `POST /saved-snapshots/{name}/shares`. The new sandbox lives in and is billed to your account. It does not get the owner's per-sandbox env; your own environment applies normally. A wrong or revoked code returns `404 snapshot_not_found`.

Each entry is a domain (`github.com`), a wildcard (`*.github.com`, which covers the domain itself and every subdomain), a public IP address or a public CIDR range. No scheme, port or path. A domain entry allows TCP 443 (matched by TLS SNI) and TCP 80 (matched by HTTP Host). An IP or CIDR entry allows every protocol and port.

inbound.description: Who can connect to the sandbox. `open`: anyone on the internet, on the ports that the sandbox opens. `boat-only`: only boat. The host drops every other connection to the sandbox, so code inside cannot make a port public. SSH, editors, port forwards, the desktop and raw ports stop: their routes answer 403 `inbound_closed`. A caller outside the sandbox (a session, or an API key that does not live in a sandbox) can still publish a port with `POST /sandboxes/{id}/host`. Commands and files through the API keep working. Omitted on PUT: the sandbox keeps what it has. Omitted on create or fork: what the sandbox inherits, else `open`. A change of `inbound` is a change of the policy: the same rules on keys and on organization environments apply. With `boat-only`, the addresses of `inboundAllow` keep SSH and raw ports.

The desktop, the browser stream, signed file URLs and `host <port>` inside the sandbox stay off: they answer 403 `inbound_closed`. A list with entries needs `inbound: boat-only` in the same request. A request that names `inbound` without `inboundAllow` empties the list. An empty list means no list. A request that names neither keeps both.

NetworkPolicyRequest.description: What the sandbox may connect to. Send `mode`, `inbound` or both: at least one. The side that the request does not name stays as it is. `inbound` and `inboundAllow` are one side. A sandbox that sets one side has its own policy and no longer follows its environment; `mode: environment` makes it follow again. On create, omitted means the policy of its environment; with `from`, the policy that the saved snapshot's sandbox had. On fork, omitted means what the source sandbox has. An API key without the `network.write` action always gets the policy that the sandbox would have without this field, a tighter one included: any other value is refused with 403 `api_key_action_forbidden`. A bad policy is refused with 400 `invalid_network_policy`. When no host can enforce a policy now, create and fork answer 409 `network_policy_unsupported`. A CI runner is always `open` and follows no environment.

mode.description: `open`: no limit. `deny`: the sandbox opens no connection. `allow`: it connects only to the entries of `allow`. `environment`: no policy of its own; the sandbox follows the policy of its environment (open when the environment sets none). This is the default on create. In an organization environment that sets a policy, only owners and admins can give a sandbox another policy: members get 403 `network_policy_managed`.

allow.description: With mode `allow`, 1 to 100 entries; empty or omitted with any other mode. An empty list with no `mode`, or with mode `open` or `deny`, means no list. Each entry is a domain (`github.com`), a wildcard (`*.github.com`, which covers the domain itself and every subdomain), a public IP address or a public CIDR range. No scheme, port or path. A domain entry allows TCP 443 (matched by TLS SNI) and TCP 80 (matched by HTTP Host). An IP or CIDR entry allows every protocol and port.

inbound.description: Who can connect to the sandbox. `open`: anyone on the internet, on the ports that the sandbox opens. `boat-only`: only boat. The host drops every other connection to the sandbox, so code inside cannot make a port public. SSH, editors, port forwards, the desktop and raw ports stop: their routes answer 403 `inbound_closed`. A caller outside the sandbox (a session, or an API key that does not live in a sandbox) can still publish a port with `POST /sandboxes/{id}/host`. Commands and files through the API keep working. Omitted on PUT: the sandbox keeps what it has. Omitted on create or fork: what the sandbox inherits, else `open`. A change of `inbound` is a change of the policy: the same rules on keys and on organization environments apply. With `boat-only`, the addresses of `inboundAllow` keep SSH and raw ports.

inboundAllow.description: The public addresses that can still connect directly to the sandbox when `inbound` is `boat-only`. Each entry is a public IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a public CIDR range. No domain, port or path. At most 50 entries. Private ranges, reserved ranges and `/0` are refused with 400 `invalid_network_policy`. A listed address reaches SSH and the raw ports of the sandbox. The desktop, the browser stream, signed file URLs and `host <port>` inside the sandbox stay off: they answer 403 `inbound_closed`. A list with entries needs `inbound: boat-only` in the same request. A request that names `inbound` without `inboundAllow` empties the list. An empty list means no list. A request that names neither keeps both.

inboundAllowAdd.description: Only on `PUT /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/network`: not on create, fork or environments. The entries to add to the list that the sandbox has. The entry rules of `inboundAllow` apply. It needs `inbound: boat-only` in the same request. Do not send it together with an `inboundAllow` that has entries. boat adds the entries when the write runs. Two callers that each add an address both keep their address. An address that another caller removed stays removed. An open sandbox becomes `boat-only` with these entries only. A result of more than 50 entries is refused with 400 `invalid_network_policy`. The answer shows the whole list in `network.inboundAllow` when the request has `include=inboundAllow`.

fileCount.description: Inventory entries alive in the chain at this generation (includes base-image system entries).

contentSizeBytes.description: Total bytes of your data restored by this snapshot (what resume/download returns; base image excluded). `null` on legacy snapshots.

contentFileCount.description: Number of your files restored by this snapshot (base image excluded). `null` on legacy snapshots.

origin.description: `template` = this Sandbox has snapshots off, so Boat never captures it: the row is a copy of the template, saved snapshot or Sandbox it was created from. `captured` = this Sandbox has snapshots on: its own captures, plus the copies Boat makes when the Sandbox is created from a source, forked or resumed.

path.description: Path relative to the snapshot root. Docker named volumes appear under `__dockervol__/`.

size.description: File size in bytes. Omitted for directories.

treeAvailable.description: `false` for legacy snapshots or inventories too large to expand; see `reason`.

truncated.description: `true` when the file list was capped; not every entry is returned.

fileCount.description: Number of your files in this snapshot (base-image system files excluded).

totalSizeBytes.description: Total bytes of your data in this snapshot (base-image system files excluded).

entries.description: Exactly the files/dirs a resume or download returns, your data only; base-image system entries are not listed.

reason.description: Why the tree is unavailable, when `treeAvailable` is `false`.

caller.description: Only when the request has `include=caller` and the sandbox has an inbound list. The caller of this request, as boat sees it.

address.description: The public address that the request comes from. Null when boat cannot tell.

listed.description: An entry of the inbound list covers `address`.

sshEndpoint.description: Public IPv4 `host:port` that forwards to the sandbox SSH server, set only when the machine has no public IPv4 of its own. Connect with `ssh -p <port> user@<host>`.

hostKey.description: The sandbox SSH server's public host key. Pin it in `known_hosts`.

StartWindowUsage.description: One rolling start window. Null when the account is unlimited.

conversationId.description: The conversation whose running turn was steered.

promptId.description: Id of the steer record. It appears in `GET /events` as a `steer` event; it is not a prompt run and has no lifecycle to poll.

native.description: `true` when the harness accepted the message into the turn that was already running, so nothing was interrupted. `false` when Boat interrupted that turn and immediately continued the SAME conversation with the instruction, which keeps the harness session and all of its memory but may repeat a little of the work in flight.

mode.description: How the message was delivered. `native` and `fallback` mirror the `native` field; `late` means the turn finished between the request and its delivery, so the message ran as an ordinary new turn on the conversation. A steer reported `native` here can settle as `native-continued` on the `steer` event: the harness accepted it but its turn ended without acting on it, so Boat continued it immediately as its own turn on the same session. Read the event for the settled mode.

id.description: Stable id of this stop. Calling stop again while it is pending returns the same id.

status.description: `pending`: accepted, the sandbox is archiving. `failing`: the last attempt failed (see `error`); it is retried automatically until the sandbox archives. Running commands or prompts does not cancel it. `completed`: the sandbox is archived. `superseded`: a resume ended it before it completed.

requestedAt.description: When the stop was accepted. On the sandbox, null once it has ended. Read by id (`GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stops/{stopId}`), it is kept.

lastAttemptAt.description: When the last archival attempt ended.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, while `status` is `failing`. Otherwise null.

endedAt.description: When the stop completed or was superseded.

forced.description: True when a force (`--force`) ended this stop. The sandbox kept its last completed snapshot, and changes after it are discarded.

type.description: Stable success envelope discriminator added by v1.

endpoint.description: The OTLP/HTTP base URL. Boat posts to `<endpoint>/v1/metrics` and `<endpoint>/v1/logs`.

headers.description: The names of the saved headers. The values are never returned.

lastExportAt.description: The time of the last metrics export that the collector accepted.

lastError.description: The most recent error from the collector, for metrics or events.

status.description: HTTP status, or null for a network error.

ok.description: True when the collector accepted the test export.

message.description: The collector error or partial-success message.

upgradedLive.description: Running sandboxes that received the new configuration now.

upgradedStopped.description: Stopped sandboxes moved to the latest version; they pick it up when they next resume.

failures.description: One entry for each sandbox that the upgrade did not move. It stays on its version, with its policy.

error.description: `network_policy_unsupported`: its host cannot enforce a policy yet. `network_policy_agent_outdated`: its agent is from before network policies. For both, stop the sandbox, then upgrade again. `network_policy_pending`: its host did not confirm the policy in time. `upgrade_failed`: another failure.

latestVersionId.description: Id of the version the sandboxes were moved to.

secret.description: Signing secret returned only when created or rotated.
